textbookText: 2. What is artery? Describe the structure of artery with labeled diagram. Ans:- Arteries are the blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart to different parts of the body. They usually carry oxygenated blood, except the pulmonary artery which carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs. The blood in arteries flows under high pressure due to the pumping action of the heart. Structure of Artery An artery has a thick and elastic wall made up of three main layers: i) Outer Layer (Tunica externa): It is made up of connective tissue that provides strength and protection to the artery. ii) Middle Layer (Tunica media): It consists of smooth muscles and elastic fibers which help the artery to stretch and withstand high pressure of blood. iii) Inner Layer (Tunica Intima): It is a smooth layer made up of epithelial cells that allows smooth flow of blood without friction. The lumen (central space) of the artery is narrow so that blood can move with high pressure.

Ans:- Diabetes: Diabetes is a metabolic disorder in which the blood sugar level remains higher than normal due to insufficient insulin production or poor utilization of insulin by the body. There are mainly three types: Type 1 (insulindependent), Type 2 (non-insulin-dependent), and gestational diabetes, which occurs during pregnancy. Common symptoms include frequent urination, excessive thirst, fatigue, weight loss, and blurred vision. If uncontrolled, it can lead to serious complications such as heart disease, kidney damage, nerve damage, and vision problems. Management includes a healthy diet, regular exercise, monitoring blood sugar, and taking medications or insulin as prescribed.

Uric Acid: Uric acid is a waste product formed from the breakdown of purines, substances found in certain foods and body cells. Normally, uric acid is excreted by the kidneys through urine, but excess levels in the blood, called hyperuricemia, can cause health problems. High uric acid can lead to gout, kidney stones, and other kidney disorders. To manage uric acid levels, it is recommended to reduce purine-rich foods like meat and seafood, drink plenty of water, maintain a healthy weight, and take medications if prescribed by a doctor. 4. Draw a labeled diagram of systemic circulation and pulmonary circulation in human body. Ans:- Pulmonary circulation: Pulmonary circulation is the pathway in which deoxygenated blood flows from the right side of the heart to the lungs and returns oxygen-rich blood to the left side of the heart. In the diagram, the right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and passes it to the right ventricle, which pumps it through the pulmonary artery to the lungs. In the lungs, blood picks up oxygen and releases carbon dioxide. The pulmonary veins then carry the oxygenated blood back to the left atrium, completing the circuit.

Systemic circulation: Systemic circulation carries oxygenated blood from the left side of the heart to the entire body and returns deoxygenated blood back to the right side of the heart. As shown in the diagram, blood moves from the left atrium to the left ventricle, which pumps it into the aorta. From the aorta, blood is distributed to all body tissues, delivering oxygen and nutrients. After exchanging gases and nutrients, the deoxygenated blood returns to the right atrium via the superior and inferior vena cava, completing the systemic loop.
